A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, with MRKE renamed IRE. All 13 pages of v1 and 24 pages of v3, including figures, tables, equations, appendices, and the later checklist, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of five LLMs on HotpotQA and edited multi-hop questions, including reasoning-chain results, ablations, and appendix sub-question results.

after.justification: v3 retains original model evaluations and reports additional factual-benchmark comparisons, data-quality scores, and an error analysis.

M1.justification: The knowledge-replacement and back-translation pipeline, QA/sub-QA generation with human review, and joint reasoning-chain evaluation remain. v1's generation prompt already requests sub-questions, so v3's clearer description of automated annotation does not establish a new method component.

E1.justification: v3 adds actual evaluations on 300 examples each from 2WikiMultihopQA and MuSiQue, substantially broadening the factual comparison beyond HotpotQA. The synthetic 2-, 3-, and 4-hop coverage remains; the newly stated total of 3600 QA pairs includes existing sub-questions rather than establishing dataset growth.

E2.justification: GPT-4, GPT-3.5, GEMINI-pro, text-davinci-003, and Bing Chat remain the evaluated models across corresponding comparisons and ablations. DisentQA and IfQA appear in v3's descriptive benchmark comparison, without reported experimental comparisons against them.

E3.justification: New evaluation procedures include GPT-4 binary correctness/informativeness scoring of sampled annotations and separate samples of 20 correct and 20 incorrect GPT-4 4-hop answers for error analysis. The retained main evaluation keeps EM/F1, temperature zero, and the existing QA prompt templates.

E4.justification: v3 adds a data-quality diagnostic using GPT-4 judgments in Table 1 and a small error analysis examining where incorrect reasoning begins and whether correct final answers conceal incorrect sub-answers in Section 4.4. These are limited extensions to the retained hopwise analyses, reasoning-chain categorization, and sub-question ablation.

E5.justification: v1 reports point estimates without specifying repeated-run counts. v3 explicitly reports averages of three experiments and introduces ± values throughout the main comparison, ablation, and appendix sub-question tables. This substantially changes uncertainty reporting, although the ± statistic is undefined and the PDFs do not establish an increase from a known earlier run count.

E6.justification: Table 3 replaces many main results: GPT-4 HotpotQA EM/F1 changes from 69.3/82.2 to 69.9/82.3, and synthetic 2-hop results from 53.2/67.7 to 53.1/62.8. New benchmark and diagnostic results are added, and v3's ablation reports 3-/4-hop sub-question benefits where v1's corresponding values were identical. Joint scores, categorical reasoning-chain percentages, and appendix sub-QA means remain unchanged. The updated scores do not establish same-setting method improvements.

T1.justification: The reasoning-chain enumeration and joint precision, recall, F1, and EM definitions are retained. Their relocation from v1's main text to v3 Appendix B introduces no new mathematical derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The central claims about edited-knowledge evaluation, joint reasoning-chain scoring, and inflated LLM performance remain. v3 modestly reframes novelty around counterfactual multi-step evaluation and describes contamination risk as reduced, whereas v1's introduction claimed its elimination.

C2.justification: v3 Section 4.5 explicitly identifies sensitivity to early sub-question errors as a limitation of joint scoring, and Appendix D flags dataset size. It retains the answer-expression limitation of exact matching but drops v1's explicit cautions about limited model coverage and incompletely reviewed GPT-4-generated data.

D1.justification: v3 documents short answer spans, answerability and coherence checks, and the accounting of 900 multi-hop questions plus 2700 sub-questions as the test set. It also changes the anonymous data-access repository target. Existing generation and evaluation prompts are retained; the added checklist does not supply concrete hardware or execution-time details.

R1.justification: Research positioning expands substantially around counterfactual QA, faithful reasoning, and benchmark leakage, adding works including DisentQA, IfQA, ReCEval, Clean-Eval, and LLMSanitize. The earlier knowledge-editing discussion citing COUNTERFACT, MQuAKE, and PokeMQA is removed, changing the relationship to prior work beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and substantial portions of the methodological narrative are rewritten. Data construction gains a nested subsection structure, related work gains thematic organization, and joint-score definitions and limitations move to appendices. New insights sections and a submission checklist further reorganize the document.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout, redraws and combines introductory illustrations, and expands the pipeline diagram. Main results and joint scores are separated, ablations gain paired with/without rows, and benchmark-property and passage-example tables are added. Existing plots are merged or relocated, alongside a new factual-versus-counterfactual comparison plot.

improvement.justification: Additional factual benchmarks, explicit data-quality checks, paired ablation tables, and three-run disclosure improve empirical coverage and transparency over v1. The net gain is limited: uncertainty values remain undefined, and the new error analysis accounts for only 18 of its 20 incorrect cases. The broader comparisons also do not directly establish contamination as the cause of the observed performance gaps.
